title: ‘The Remarried Empress’ Shatters Disney+ & Hulu Records as Biggest Local Original Launch Ever
body:
The Korean drama “The Remarried Empress” has shattered streaming records, becoming the most‑watched local original premiere in Disney+ and Hulu’s history across more than 50 territories, including the United States, United Kingdom, France, Germany and Mexico. The romantic epic, headlined by Shin Mina, Ju Ji‑hoon, Lee Jong‑suk and Lee Se‑young, drew unprecedented viewership numbers on its debut weekend, positioning the series as Disney’s most successful non‑English launch to date.

The series, adapted from a popular web novel and webtoon, follows the political and emotional turbulence of a queen who, after a bitter divorce, remarries a rival monarch to safeguard her kingdom. Its blend of court intrigue, lavish production design and contemporary romance resonated with a global audience that has increasingly embraced Korean content. In its first three days, “The Remarried Empress” logged more than 30 million viewing hours on Disney+ and Hulu combined, surpassing the previous record set by the Korean thriller “Squid Game” on the same platforms. The surge was especially notable in markets where Korean dramas have traditionally been niche, indicating a shift in consumer appetite for high‑budget, culturally specific storytelling.

Industry analysts attribute the triumph to several converging factors. First, Disney’s aggressive rollout strategy—simultaneously releasing the series in over 50 regions with localized subtitles and dubbing—ensured that language barriers did not impede access. Second, the star power of Shin Mina, a veteran actress with a strong fan base across Asia, and Ju Ji‑hoon, whose recent roles have broadened his international profile, generated buzz on social media platforms such as TikTok, Twitter and Instagram. Third, the timing of the launch coincided with a lull in new content from competing streaming services, allowing “The Remarried Empress” to dominate the recommendation algorithms and capture viewer attention during a high‑traffic weekend.

The success also underscores Disney’s broader strategy to diversify its content library beyond its traditional Western franchises. Over the past two years, the company has invested heavily in Asian productions, commissioning original series in Japan, India and South Korea. The record‑setting performance of “The Remarried Empress” validates that approach, proving that localized stories can achieve global reach when backed by a platform with Disney’s distribution muscle. Moreover, the series’ strong performance on both Disney+ and Hulu demonstrates the synergy between the two services, with Hulu’s U.S. audience contributing a sizable share of the total viewership.

While the numbers are impressive, they also raise questions about sustainability. Critics note that the streaming market is becoming increasingly saturated, and maintaining momentum for non‑English titles will require consistent quality and strategic marketing. Disney’s next steps will likely involve leveraging the series’ popularity to expand the franchise—potentially through spin‑offs, merchandise or even a live‑action adaptation—mirroring the multi‑platform exploitation seen with other hit properties. Additionally, the company may double down on data‑driven content acquisition, using the viewership metrics from “The Remarried Empress” to inform future investments in Korean dramas and other regional productions.

Looking ahead, “The Remarried Empress” could set a new benchmark for how global streaming giants approach local original content. If Disney can replicate this model across other markets, it may reshape the competitive landscape, compelling rivals to prioritize culturally resonant storytelling over generic, globally‑targeted series. For now, the drama’s record‑breaking debut signals a clear appetite among international audiences for richly crafted, regionally rooted narratives, and positions Disney+ and Hulu as leading platforms for delivering such content to a worldwide viewership.
